name: Active Object
intent: Give an object its own thread and a queue, so that callers submit requests and carry on, and the object handles them one at a time.
scenario: Many threads use a calculator service that keeps a history of results. The history is not safe to touch from two threads at once.
problem: Every caller runs the method on its own thread, so the shared history needs locks, and callers wait for their turn on the lock. One slow request holds up the callers behind it, and a missed lock somewhere makes the history wrong.
solution: An ActiveCalculator stands in front of the real calculator (the servant). Calling add() does not run it: the call is turned into a request, put on a queue, and a future is returned at once. One worker thread takes requests from the queue and runs them on the servant one after another. Only that thread ever touches the servant's data, so it needs no locks. Callers carry on and read the result from the future when they need it.
pain: The servant's shared state needs locks, and one missing lock is a bug
Callers are blocked while they wait for the lock
One slow call delays every caller waiting behind it
Which thread runs a method depends on who called it
benefits: The servant's state is touched by one thread only, so it needs no locks
Callers do not wait for the method to run: they get a future at once (unless a bounded queue is full)
With a FIFO queue, as here, requests are handled in the order they were submitted
Concurrency is hidden behind an ordinary-looking interface
whenToUse: An object holds state that many threads need, and locking it everywhere is error-prone
Callers should not block while the work is done
Work should happen in order, such as logging, a device driver or a UI
whenNotToUse: Fast, simple operations where a lock would be cheaper than a queue and a thread
Work that must run in parallel on several cores: one worker runs one request at a time
When callers need the result right away on every call: they wait on the future anyway
pitfalls: An unbounded queue grows without limit when callers are faster than the worker
A request that waits for a future from its own object deadlocks, because the only worker is busy waiting
One slow request delays every request behind it, because there is only one worker
An error inside the worker must travel back through the future, or the caller never learns of it

roles.label: Proxy
roles.description: The interface callers see. Each call becomes a request on the queue and returns a future.

roles.label: Scheduler
roles.description: The queue and the single worker thread that takes requests and runs them in order.

roles.label: Servant
roles.description: The real object with the real logic. Only the worker thread ever calls it.

roles.label: Future
roles.description: Where the caller later reads the result, or the error, of its request.

quiz.question: Eight threads share a service whose state is not thread-safe. They guard every method with one lock, and callers spend much of their time waiting for it. What is the best change?
options: Give each thread its own copy of the service, and merge the copies once a day
Use a finer lock on every single field, so that more of the threads can get in at once
Put an active object in front of it: queue the requests, run them on one worker, and return futures
Call the service only from the busiest thread, and ask the other threads to wait for it
quiz.explanation: With an active object the service's state is used by one worker only, so it needs no locks, and callers continue straight away with a future. Separate copies produce different state, finer locks add complexity, and routing everything through one busy thread blocks the rest.

quiz.question: During a traffic spike, callers submit requests faster than the worker can handle them. The queue grows until the process runs out of memory. What is the best fix?
options: Bound the queue, and decide what happens when it is full: block, reject or drop the oldest
Make the queue larger by giving the process more memory, so that it can hold every spike
Remove the queue, and let the callers run the requests on their own threads again
Process requests in a random order, so that no single caller fills the queue
quiz.explanation: An unbounded queue turns overload into an out-of-memory crash. A bounded queue makes the overload visible and forces a decision about what to do with the extra. More memory only delays the failure, and removing the queue brings back the locks.

quiz.question: A servant method calls another method on its own active-object proxy and waits for the result. The service then hangs. What happened?
options: The queue was full, so the second request was rejected and the first was left waiting
The second call went to a different worker, which was waiting for the first to finish
The future was created too late, so the result arrived before there was anywhere to put it
The only worker is waiting for a request that only that worker can run, so it waits for itself
quiz.explanation: One worker runs one request at a time. If the running request waits for a new request that sits behind it in the queue, nothing can ever finish. Inside the servant, call the method directly, or continue with a callback instead of waiting.
